;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Moro conflict]]
**During a shootout with soldiers in [[Sulu]], [[Philippines]], [[Abu Sayyaf]] militants kills an [[Indonesia]]n fisherman who was abducted early this year. A militant of the group also died in the fight. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/10/01/news/regions/kidnapped-indon-fisherman-killed-in-sulu/774368/ (''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)|Iraqi insurgency]]
**[[2020 Iraq attacks]]
***A missile hits a house in [[Baghdad]], close to the [[Baghdad International Airport|airport]]. The attack leaves at least five people dead, including three children; two children are injured. [http://ninanews.com/Website/News/Details?Key=859530 (National Iraqi News Agency)]
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
***Seventy-one more [[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]] servicemen are killed during the fight, bringing the death toll among the fighters to 87. Two more Azerbaijani civilians are also killed. A passenger bus in [[Armenia]] was hit by an Azerbaijani missile, but no casualties are reported. Authorities in Nagorno reports at least 400 Azerbaijani soldiers dead, but the country has not confirmed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54338454 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Kioxia]], the [[Japan]]ese [[computer memory]] manufacturer [[Corporate spin-off|spun off]] from [[Toshiba]], postpones its [[initial public offering]] on the [[Tokyo Stock Exchange]], citing the volatility of the [[semiconductor]] industry caused by both the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and the [[China–United States trade war|ongoing trade war]] between [[China]] and the [[United States]]. Its initial public offering, which would have launched on October 6, was projected to be Japan's largest for this year. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/09/28/business/corporate-business/toshiba-chip-kioxia-tokyo-bourse/ (''The Japan Times'')] [https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics/International-relations/US-China-tensions/Japanese-chipmaker-Kioxia-delays-IPO-amid-US-China-tensions (NikkeAsia)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[India]] surpasses six million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], becoming the second country after the [[United States]] to reach that milestone. Meanwhile, 82.5% or more than five million people have recovered. [https://apnews.com/article/virus-outbreak-india-archive-eb878bbd69a165e9e64771b5746fea62 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
***The [[Government of the Netherlands|government]] introduces new nationwide restrictions aimed at tackling the swift spread sweeping across the country, including disallowing fans in professional sports matches and ordering bars and restaurants to close at 22:00 (10:00 p.m.) CEST for the next three weeks. [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] also advises people to wear face masks when shopping in [[Amsterdam]], [[Rotterdam]], and [[The Hague]], the three cities with the highest rates of infections. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/dutch-government-announces-new-restrictions-to-rein-in-virus-1.5123515 (CTV News)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of the Dominican Republic]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]]'s Foreign Ministry [[dismissal (employment)|fires]] 781 people in various [[Diplomatic mission|embassies]]. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/09/28/foreign-ministry-fires-781-cuts-us45-7m-of-gov-fat-yearly/ (''Dominican Today'')]
*[[Papua conflict]], [[Foreign relations of Indonesia]], [[Foreign relations of Vanuatu]]
**[[Indonesia]] accuses [[Vanuatu]] of having an "excessive and unhealthy obsession" about [[Western New Guinea|West Papua]]. The remark comes after [[Prime Minister of Vanuatu|Vanuatuan Prime Minister]] [[Bob Loughman]] warned the international community about "human rights violations and abuses" in the region. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/427114/indonesia-lashes-out-at-vanuatu-over-west-papua-at-the-un (RNZ)]
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
**[[Russia]] announces that they have supplied their first batch of their [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V]] vaccine to [[Belarus]] for clinical trails. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-russia-vaccine-belaru/russia-supplies-covid-19-vaccine-to-belarus-for-clinical-trials-idUSR4N2FT01F (Reuters)]

;Law and crime	
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]], [[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Spain|Spanish Supreme Court]] ratifies a year-and-a-half disqualification sentence to [[President of the Government of Catalonia]] [[Quim Torra]]. He must abandon the presidency after being accused of disobeying the [[Junta Electoral Central|Central Electoral Bureau]]. [[List of vice presidents of Catalonia|Vice president]] [[Pere Aragonès]] will succeed him ''ad interim'' effective September 29. [https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2020/09/28/5f70ebbefc6c83fe188b4613.html (''El Mundo'')] [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-spain-politics-catalonia-idUKKBN26J1NJ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54328334 (BBC News)]
**Demonstrations take place throughout [[Catalonia]], as well as protests in [[Barcelona]]. [https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/cataluna/2020-09-28/protesta-barcelona-inhabilitacion-torra-lanzan-petardos-mossos_2766356/ (''El Confidencial'')] [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200928/483741765014/manifestaciones-cataluna-barcelona-protestas-ihabilitacion-torra-ayuntamientos.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*[[Corruption in Pakistan]]
**[[Leader of the Opposition (Pakistan)|Leader of the Opposition]] [[Shehbaz Sharif]] is arrested amid a corruption scandal. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/9/28/pakistan-opposition-leader-arrested-in-corruption-case (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*Three ministers resign from [[Bolivia]]'s interim [[government of Bolivia|government]]. One of them, Economic Minister Oscar Ortiz, stated his resignation was in protest of [[President of Bolivia|President]] [[Jeanine Áñez]]'s decision to sell shares in the state-run electricity company ELFEC close to the [[2020 Bolivian general election|upcoming general election]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/bolivia-key-ministers-resign-ahead-of-presidential-elections/a-55086390 (DW)]

;Science and technology
*[[Water on Mars]]
**Scientists in a paper published to ''[[Nature Astronomy]]'' confirm the existence of four underground saltwater lakes spread out over {{convert|75000|sqkm|sqmi}} near [[Mars]]' [[Planum Australe|south pole]]. Depending on their salt content, these lakes could be potential holders of [[Life on Mars|life]]. [https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-02751-1 (''Nature'')]
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**[[CHEOPS]] announces the observation of [[WASP-189 b|WASP-189b]], an ultra-[[Hot Jupiter]] exoplanet that orbits the star HD 133112 (also known as WASP-189) 322-light years away from the [[Libra (constellation)|Libra]] constellation. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/28/world/ultra-hot-exoplanet-esa-cheops-scn-trnd/index.html (CNN)]

;Sports
*[[2020 Stanley Cup playoffs]]
**[[2020 Stanley Cup Finals]]
***The [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] win the [[Stanley Cup]] for the first time since [[2004 Stanley Cup Finals|2004]] following their game 6 victory against the [[Dallas Stars]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nhl/2020/09/28/lightning-beat-stars-game-6-win-stanley-cup/3551980001/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[FIFA]] gives the president of the [[Club Olimpia]] of [[Paraguay]] Marco Trovato a lifetime ban from all [[Association football|football]]-related activity, following an investigation into match manipulation. He is also fined [[Swiss franc|CHF]]100,000. Trovato said he would appeal the decision. [https://www.fifa.com/who-we-are/news/the-fifa-disciplinary-committee-sanctions-marco-antonio-trovato-villalba-for-mat (FIFA)] [https://es.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-paraguay-matchfixing-idUKKBN26J26O (Reuters)]
